X.note: The street and walls are strong, photoreal-looking CGI. The figures are mannequin-like game assets with a stiff walk and a clumsy mid-stride pose. Blue-trousered figures with bare bald heads look like unfinished models. The mid-street cluster of redcoats is a repetitive, overlapping blob. Cross-belts, caps and the flag are generic and plausibly period at best. The lone shadow on the ground has no clear source.

Y.note: Same strong environment. The figures stand in a stiff, posed lineup like painted figurines or cardboard cutouts, with no motion and an odd white-gown figure at the centre. Several figures have no feet or sit on pegs. A dark civilian in a hat stands isolated. The posed groups look marginally more coherent and period-readable than X's blob. Their uniform colours and white breeches are closer to a plausible 1782 look. The shadows are detached from the figures.

why: The environment is identical, and Y's figures are a little more readable and period-plausible, but both are toy-like and Y is only marginally better.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the mannequin figures in X with properly scaled, varied period soldiers (tricorne or round hats, correct coats, breeches and gaiters) in natural marching poses. Add grounded contact shadows and spread them out so they don't blob together.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack flag with the 1801 design (the 1782 Union flag had no St Patrick's cross)
Bare bald heads and blue trousers on X's figures, which suggest unfinished or mismatched models
Figures with pegs or no feet
Generic cross-belts and caps on the soldiers
